battle.name: 戊辰戰爭
battle.brief: 一八六八年一月三日江戶城不戰而開，幕府軍退守大坂，鳥羽伏見與大坂之戰接連失利，五月北走越前敦賀，六月二十七日蝦夷共和國投降。卡面雷管步槍正是官軍壓過幕府鳥銃的底火槍械，十八式小銃由小石川工場仿製，定裝藥莢帶來的射速與射程，把守軍的密集隊形變成活靶。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries: 戊辰戰爭的交戰雙方，是一八六八年一月建立的新政府軍（史稱官軍）與仍握兵權的江戶幕府軍。官軍方面，朝廷在元年正月設軍務總督，由東久邇宮載淳總裁，參議五條實美與岩倉具視分掌民政，以大久保利通為兵部大輔掌軍政；兵分三路，東海道軍坐鎮中部，東道軍由大村益次郎節制軍務、山縣有朋領先鋒，西道軍以西鄉隆盛所率薩摩兵與長州兵為主力，在淀川兩岸與海淀一線作戰；另由桂久武率四百名洋槍隊與數門野戰炮，乘軍艦咸臨丸自大阪直取江戶，因懸掛美國旗而未遭沿途炮擊。各藩的倒幕義師陸續歸隊，薩摩、長州兩藩兵是最大宗兵力，其餘二十餘藩以士族為主的義勇軍編入。幕府軍方面，慶喜以總帥身分把直轄的步兵、砲兵與洋槍隊帶往大坂，交彥坂總守德川茂德坐鎮大坂城；江戶由守備總督德川家達與新選組、彰武隊等警衛；十月大政奉還之後，仍有名家與浪人自願加入，五月北撤時組成號稱五列車的四千餘人隊伍，帶著大砲與輜重沿東海道北上。戰局末段，幕府又與會津、仙台、米澤組成的東北同盟合流，退往奧羽、越中、北陸，最後退守北海道。元年一月，箱館方面另建以榊莫齊為總統、鍋島若狹守為副總統的蝦夷共和國，與官軍對抗至同年六月。
countriesEn: The two sides in the Boshin War were the new government army set up in January 1868, historically called the imperial forces, and the army of the Edo shogunate, which still held the guns. On the government side the court established a supreme commander of military affairs in the first month of the first year of Meiji, with Prince Higashikuni Naritomo as its president, the councillors Sanjō Sanetomi and Iwakura Tomomi taking charge of civil administration, and Ōkubo Toshimichi as minister of war. The army was split into three columns: the Tōkaidō army covering the centre, the eastern army under Ōmura Masujirō for the conduct of operations with Yamagata Aritomo commanding the vanguard, and the western army with Saigō Tsugumichi's Satsuma and Chōshū troops as its main body, fighting along both banks of the Yodo and on the line of Haidian. Separately, Katsu Kaishu took four hundred riflemen and several field guns aboard the warship Kankō Maru from Osaka straight for Edo, and because the ship flew the American ensign she was not fired on by the coastal batteries on the way. The levies of the other domains joined the columns as they advanced, the contingents of Satsuma and Chōshū being the largest single bodies, with the rest of the twenty-odd domains contributing irregular companies of samurai. On the shogunate side, Yoshinobu as supreme commander took the shogunate's own infantry, artillery and foreign-drill rifle corps to Osaka and left the defence of Osaka castle to Tokugawa Shigetoku, the lord of Hikone; in Edo the guard was entrusted to the shogunate's governor Tokugawa Iesato, with the Shinsengumi and the Shōbu-tai among the defenders. Even after the restoration of rule to the court in October, great lords and masterless swordsmen continued to volunteer, and when the army withdrew north in May it formed the so-called five trains, a body of more than four thousand men dragging the heavy guns and the baggage up the Tōkaidō. Late in the war the shogunate joined the Tōhoku alliance of Aizu, Sendai and Yonezawa, retreating through Dewa, Echizen and Kaga before making its last stand in Hokkaidō. In January 1868 a separate state, the Republic of Ezo, was proclaimed at Hakodate with Enomoto Takeaki as president and Nabeshima Wakasano-kami as vice-president, and it resisted the imperial troops until June of the same year.
people: 關西的指揮核心是薩摩與長州。西鄉隆盛以薩摩藩軍事統帥的身分率兵北上，五月受任征伐大總督，七月十四日率部入江戶，在京城的居留前後三個月；山縣有朋率先鋒隊在伏見撕開缺口，其後出任別動隊總督進入東北，再以北海道總督的身分統率箱館的第二次總攻擊；大村益次郎掌東道軍務，制定槍隊操法與陣形，並在一八六八年二月造出三輪軍用車以運輸槍械與彈藥，卻在沼津附近的刀爾之坂遇伏，重傷後於二月十三日不治。大久保利通掌兵部與財政，後來在廢藩置縣與地租改革的籌畫中扮演主角。幕府方面的核心是德川慶喜與德川茂德：慶喜在江戶城開城後退守大坂，一月二十七日鳥羽伏見之戰率約三千人出戰而敗，五月九日大坂城陷落時北走，在米澤棲身，翌年返回江戶。會津方面由藩主松平容保出任東北同盟的軍事總帥，其家臣照月圓爾主張恭順而被幕府處刑。土方久成以土方歲三之弟的身分率島義兵入主箱館，與榊莫齊、島義行共同守備蝦夷地，榊莫齊於六月二十七日代表蝦夷共和國投降。勝海舟是官軍與幕府留守勢力之間的居間者，坂本龍馬與中岡慎太郎在一八六七年前後穿梭各藩勸說舉兵，中岡慎太郎於土佐戰死、坂本龍馬在京都遇刺。法國方面，一八六七年抵日的軍事顧問團由上尉朱爾·布內率領，全團不足二十人，在兵庫操練官軍；前法國海軍工程官雷奧納·韋爾尼受幕府聘用，在橫濱建造船所、訓練砲術隊，並替幕府向法國訂購槍械。一八六八年九月五日，遠東法國艦隊司令勒翁·羅茲為迫使幕府的關門砲台停火，炮擊下關的砲台。
peopleEn: The command core of the western side lay in Satsuma and Chōshū. Saigō Tsugumichi led the Satsuma troops north as the domain's military commander, was appointed supreme commander of the campaign in May, and entered Edo with his force on 14 July, remaining in the capital for about three months. Yamagata Aritomo tore open the front at Fushimi as commander of the vanguard, afterwards went north as commander of the separate columns, and finally directed the second general assault on Hakodate as governor of the Hokkaidō expedition. Ōmura Masujirō handled the military affairs of the eastern column, worked out the drill and formations of the new rifle, and in February 1868 built a tricycle gun carriage for moving muskets and ammunition; he was ambushed on the Sengen road near Numazu, was mortally wounded, and died on 13 February. Ōkubo Toshimichi held the ministry of war and the treasury and would later be the driving force behind the reform of the domains and of the land tax. On the shogunate side the key men were Tokugawa Yoshinobu and Tokugawa Shigetoku. After Edo castle was opened without a battle Yoshinobu fell back on Osaka, marched out with some three thousand men on 27 January for the battle of Toba and Fushimi, and was defeated; when Osaka castle fell on 9 May he went north and stayed at Yonezawa, returning to Edo the following year. On the Aizu side the domain lord Matsudaira Katamori was named military commander of the Tōhoku alliance, and his retainer Terutsuki Enji, who urged submission, was executed on the shogunate's orders. Hijikata Hisanari, the younger brother of Hijikata Toshizō, led the Ezo volunteers into Hakodate and shared the defence of the northern country with Enomoto Takeaki and Shimamura Yoshiyuki; Enomoto surrendered on behalf of the Republic of Ezo on 27 June. Katsu Kaishu acted as the intermediary between the government forces and the shogunate's own garrison in Edo, while Sakamoto Ryōma and Nakaoka Shintarō travelled among the domains in 1867 urging them to rise; Nakaoka was killed in Tosa and Sakamoto was assassinated in Kyoto. On the French side, the military mission that arrived in 1867 was led by Captain Jules Brunet and numbered fewer than twenty men in all; it drilled the government troops at Hyōgo. Léonce Verny, a former French naval engineer, was employed by the shogunate to build a shipyard at Yokohama, to train the artillery crews, and to order weapons from France. On 5 September 1868 Admiral Léon Roze, commanding the French squadron in the Far East, shelled the batteries at Shimonoseki in order to force the shogunate's shore guns to cease fire.
kits: 卡面這件雷管步槍，是戊辰戰爭裡決定火力差距的東西。官軍一側，雷管式步槍以法國人沙美爾與德爾維涅設計的兩個型號落實：十三式是口徑十一點五毫米、全長約九百一十四毫米的三尺短槍，十八式是口徑七點五毫米、全長約一千五百二十毫米的五尺長槍，一八六六至一八六八年間在小石川工場仿製，工場本身有法國顧問指導。與之配套的是定裝藥莢，底火、火藥與彈丸合裝於一紙殼之內，士兵不必再在霧氣與黑煙裡分裝底火與散藥，這是官軍射擊速度高於幕府散裝彈的關鍵。幕府一側則有三個來源：鳥銃與管打火繩槍佔多數，由薩摩、長州等藩的兵器庫改裝；英製恩菲爾德步槍與英製後膛炮由會津藩經橫濱的洋行取得，數量約千支步槍與數門炮；法製槍械由幕府直接向法國訂購，數量以萬計，另有十餘門野戰炮與一批沿岸防禦用重炮，經海運分批抵日，一部分在兵庫與九州被官軍截留。炮兵是雙方差距最大的一環：官軍在淀川兩岸與箱館的殘丘上以野戰炮壓制守軍，長州藩幕末輸入的五門西式大炮在鳥羽伏見即已投入使用；幕府的海防線上則有配備重炮的關門、姬路等砲台，射程遠但固定而無機動。此外，官軍以兼備蒸汽與帆力的咸臨丸運兵，並以海路把兵員與彈藥自大阪運到江戶與箱館；蝦夷共和國則在舊金山購得三桅帆船開洋丸充作軍艦，並以英美籍顧問組成參謀部。未及上陣的新政府軍在箱館作戰時，攜帶的彈藥只夠支撐十餘日，砲彈、藥莢與馬匹飼料的短缺，比任何單件兵器都更直接左右了攻勢的長短。
kitsEn: The percussion rifle on this card is the piece that decided the margin of firepower in the Boshin War. On the government side the percussion musket arrived in two French patterns designed by Chamel and Delvigne: the Type 13 was a three-shaku carbine of 11.5 mm calibre and about 914 mm in length, the Type 18 a five-shaku rifle of 7.5 mm calibre and about 1,520 mm in length. Both were copied at the Koishikawa arsenal between 1866 and 1868, and the arsenal itself was built with French advice. What went with them was the fixed ammunition cartridge, in which primer, charge and ball were packed together in a single paper case, so that the soldier no longer had to fit a primer and loose powder in fog and gun smoke; that was the reason the government troops could fire faster than the shogunate's loose ammunition. The shogunate's weapons came from three directions. Matchlocks and tube-fired flint guns were the majority, converted in the arsenals of domains such as Satsuma and Chōshū. British Enfield muskets and British breech-loading guns were obtained by the Aizu domain through foreign merchants at Yokohama, to the tune of roughly a thousand muskets and several guns. French weapons were ordered directly by the shogunate from France, tens of thousands of them, together with a dozen-odd field guns and a batch of heavy coastal pieces; they came by sea in several shipments, and part of them was seized by the government troops at Hyōgo and in Kyūshū. Artillery was by far the widest gap between the two sides: the government used field guns to batter the defenders on both banks of the Yodo and on the heights above Hakodate, and the five Western guns the Chōshū domain had imported at the end of the shogunate were already in action at Toba and Fushimi. The shogunate's coastal line, by contrast, carried heavy guns in batteries at Shimonoseki and Himeji, long in range but fixed and without manoeuvre. Beyond the small arms, the government moved troops in the steam-and-sail Kankō Maru and carried men and ammunition by sea from Osaka to Edo and to Hakodate, while the Republic of Ezo had bought the three-masted barque Kaiyō Maru in San Francisco to serve as a warship and staffed a general staff with British and American advisers. And the ammunition was what the new army could not get enough of: the force that fought at Hakodate carried barely more than a fortnight's supply, and the shortage of gunpowder, cartridges and horse fodder told the length of any advance more directly than any single weapon did.
tactics: 官軍的戰法是西式操典加火砲，與幕府的密集亂戰完全不同。元年一月三日，桂久武乘咸臨丸在品川外海豎起旗幟，勝海舟居間與幕府留守方談判，江戶城未經交火即開，兵不血刃地拿下關東的耳目與物資。四路進攻的關鍵是鳥羽伏見：一月二十七日拂曉，山縣有朋率先鋒自南面突入伏見，廣幡忠勇與西鄉隆盛的薩摩兵同時自西面壓上鳥羽，兩翼在濕冷的清晨同時開火；幕府約三千人雖有十數門火炮，卻因各陣互不接應而崩解，慶喜退回大坂。大坂之戰自四月重啟：官軍先用野戰炮壓制城外的射手，再以步兵逐次奪取生野、難波等外圍陣地，五月合圍大坂，炮擊城壁與天滿橋周邊，殘存守軍在連續突擊中耗盡，遂於五月九日城破，慶喜乘船沿淀川北走，隨後的五列車把火炮、輜重與部隊沿東海道推向敦賀與金澤。幕府的戰術則是密集隊形加近戰：一八六八年五月的北撤途中，會津、新選組等部在黑暗中反覆襲擊官軍縱隊，以近身白刃與短射程槍械強迫敵軍收縮，但這種打法在官軍的散兵線與步槍射程前一再失效。箱館之役最能顯示高低差與火砲的威力：官軍第一次攻擊定頭山時，蝦夷方佔據高處，以槍砲俯射登山的官軍，攻方在斜坡上死傷慘重而退；第二次總攻擊改以砲兵先行掩護，步兵分段躍進，六月攻下定頭山與山麓的砲台，再逼向箱館城下，最後以夜襲與圍城迫使蝦夷政府於六月二十七日投降。整場戰爭的分水嶺，是射程、藥莢與彈藥存量，而不是雙方的白刃戰。
tacticsEn: The government's way of fighting was Western drill supported by artillery, and nothing like the shogunate's massed close combat. On 3 January 1868 Katsu Kaishu raised his flag from the Kankō Maru off Shinagawa, and with Katsu acting as intermediary he negotiated with the shogunate's garrison; Edo castle was opened without a shot, and the government took the communications and the stores of Kantō for nothing. The hinge of the campaign was the battle of Toba and Fushimi. In the dawn of 27 January Yamagata Aritomo's vanguard broke in from the south at Fushimi while Hirohata Tadayoshi and Saigō Tsugumichi's Satsuma troops came on at Toba from the west, and both wings opened fire in the wet cold of the morning. The shogunate's three thousand men, with perhaps a dozen guns between them, fell apart because their formations did not support one another, and Yoshinobu withdrew to Osaka. The battle for Osaka was resumed in April: the government first used its field guns to silence the skirmishers outside the walls, then took the outer positions at Ikuno and Namba step by step with infantry, closed around the city in May, and shelled the walls and the ground around Tenmabashi until the remnants of the garrison were spent in repeated attacks. The castle fell on 9 May, Yoshinobu went north by boat on the Yodo, and the five trains carried the guns, the baggage and the men up the Tōkaidō towards Tsuruga and Kanazawa. The shogunate's method was dense formations and close fighting: on the northward retreat in May 1868 Aizu and Shinsengumi parties made repeated night attacks on the government columns, forcing the enemy to close up with the bayonet and with short-ranged muskets, but such attacks failed again and again against the government skirmish line and the reach of the rifle. The battle for Hakodate shows most clearly what height and artillery were worth. When the government first attacked the heights of Teitoyama, the Ezo side held the high ground and shot down the troops climbing the slope, and the attackers were badly cut up and withdrew. The second general assault reversed the order: the guns opened first to cover the advance, the infantry moved forward by bounds, and in June the heights of Teitoyama and the batteries at their foot were taken, the push going on to the castle below, until night attacks and siege brought the Ezo government to surrender on 27 June. The divide in the whole war was range, cartridges and the amount of ammunition in the magazine, not the bayonet work in the field.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。戰爭自一八六八年一月三日江戶城開城起，到同年六月二十七日蝦夷共和國投降為止，約五個半月、一百七十六日；若計到一八六九年一月的箱館灣海戰與土方久成陣亡，前後近十三個月。兵力方面，官軍在關西集結時約一萬至一萬五千人，其中薩摩、長州兩藩兵佔大頭，其餘為各藩義師；幕府直轄部隊與大名聯軍約八千至一萬人，五月北撤的五列車約四千人。鳥羽伏見一役，官軍實際投入約三千至五千人、野戰炮十餘門，幕府軍約三千人；官軍陣亡數百人，幕府軍死傷逾二千，其中大批是受傷後失血或火藥灼傷不治。大坂之戰四月至五月，官軍動員數萬人、大砲數十門，五月九日城破時幕府軍主力損失慘重。箱館方面，第二次總攻擊的官軍約五千人、野戰炮十餘門，蝦夷共和國一方約三千人（含島義兵約一千八百人），官軍陣亡數百人、蝦夷方陣亡約千人。距離上，江戶至箱館約一千六百公里海路，大阪至敦賀約二百公里，箱館至松前約十五公里。武器方面，十八式小銃口徑七點五毫米、全長約一千五百二十毫米，十三式口徑十一點五毫米、全長約九百一十四毫米；法國軍事顧問團一八六七年抵日時全團十八人左右；幕府向法國的槍械訂購以萬計，另有十餘門野戰炮；會津藩另自英國商行取得英製步槍約千支與英製後膛炮數門。各家日文史料對兵員與傷亡的記載差異頗大，上述數字應視為量級而非定論。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The war lasted from the opening of Edo castle on 3 January 1868 to the surrender of the Republic of Ezo on 27 June of the same year, about five and a half months and one hundred and seventy-six days; counting the battle of Hakodate Bay and the death of Hijikata Hisanari in January 1869, the whole business came to nearly thirteen months. In men, the government had assembled in Kansai perhaps ten to fifteen thousand, the bulk of them the troops of the Satsuma and Chōshū domains and the rest the levies of the other domains; the shogunate's own troops and the contingents of the great lords numbered about eight to ten thousand, and the five trains that withdrew north in May carried some four thousand. In the battle of Toba and Fushimi the government actually engaged three to five thousand men with a dozen-odd field guns against about three thousand shogunate troops; the government lost several hundred dead, and the shogunate's dead and wounded exceeded two thousand, a large part of them men who bled to death after being hit or were burned by powder. In the fighting for Osaka from April to May the government mobilised tens of thousands and dozens of guns, and the shogunate's main body was badly mauled when the castle fell on 9 May. At Hakodate the government brought about five thousand men and a dozen-odd field guns against the second general assault, while the Republic of Ezo had about three thousand, the Ezo volunteers numbering roughly one thousand eight hundred; the government lost several hundred dead and the Ezo side about a thousand. In distance, Edo and Hakodate are about one thousand six hundred kilometres apart by sea, Osaka and Tsuruga about two hundred kilometres, and Hakodate and Matsumae about fifteen. In weapons, the Type 18 rifle had a calibre of 7.5 mm and a length of about 1,520 mm, the Type 13 a calibre of 11.5 mm and a length of about 914 mm; the French military mission numbered about eighteen men when it arrived in 1867; the shogunate's order from France ran to tens of thousands of muskets with a dozen-odd field guns; and the Aizu domain separately obtained about a thousand British muskets and several British breech-loading guns through merchants in Yokohama. Japanese sources differ considerably on the numbers of men and casualties, and the figures above should be read as orders of magnitude rather than as settled fact.
cause: 打起來的原因是多層累積的。最底層是幕府的財政與生計：十九世紀前期反覆的歉收讓幕藩體系的年貢難以支應，人口壓力與米價高漲使農村與町人同時困頓，幕末多次的藩政改革與賑濟都沒有觸及根源。上一層是開國帶來的外部衝擊：一八五三年美國使節抵日，一八五八年日美修好通商條約簽訂，江戶、大阪、橫濱開港，日本被捲入以生絲為主的國際貿易，進口品擠壓傳統手工業，幕府又向外舉借而背上巨額外債，錢糧與軍需的出海口大半被洋商與開港地的新商業網控制。第三層是尊王攘夷到倒幕的政治轉向：志士最初以攘夷為口號，一八六四年蛤濱門的戰事與一八六六年第二次長州征討之後，他們明白單憑孤忠與死力不足，轉而謀求同樣握有資產與炮兵的大藩合作，坂本龍馬與中岡慎太郎在一八六七年前後往返各藩與京都之間，最終促成了倒幕派的密議，標誌著倒幕派與薩摩、長州之間的聯合。第四層是幕府自身的轉變：慶喜在英法借款與海軍近代化上投入甚多，新式軍隊與外國顧問卻同時成了新政府的助力；在兵部大輔等官員的推動下，一八六七年十月十四日慶喜上表請將政權奉還朝廷。直接導火線在元年正月：幕府主動開了江戶城，慶喜於十日上辭表，京城的勢力隨即接管關東與兵庫，而鳥羽伏見的失敗讓幕府已無力抵抗成為定局，戰爭自此再無停止的可能。
causeEn: The reasons for fighting were accumulated in layers. The deepest was the shogunate's finances and the conditions of the people. Repeated bad harvests in the early nineteenth century made the annual tribute of the domains impossible to meet; population pressure and high rice prices pinched farmers and townsmen at once, and the reforms and relief measures of the late shogunate never touched the root of it. Above that lay the external shock of the opening of the country: the American envoy arrived in 1853, the Treaty of Amity and Commerce was signed in 1858, and Edo, Osaka and Yokohama were opened, drawing Japan into an international trade centred on raw silk. Imports undercut the traditional handicrafts, the shogunate borrowed heavily abroad and loaded itself with foreign debt, and the outlets for money and military supply passed largely into the hands of the foreign merchants and the new commercial networks of the treaty ports. The third layer was the political turn from sonnō jōei to the overthrow of the shogunate. The activists began with exclusion of foreigners as their slogan, but after the fighting at the Hamaguri Gate in 1864 and the second expedition against Chōshū in 1866 they understood that loyalty and courage alone were not enough, and turned instead to seek the alliance of the great domains that held the money and the guns. The travels of Sakamoto Ryōma and Nakaoka Shintarō among the domains and Kyoto in 1866 and 1867 produced the secret talks that bound the overthrowers to Satsuma and Chōshū. The fourth layer was the shogunate's own transformation. Yoshinobu spent heavily on British and French loans and on modernising the navy, and the new-style troops and foreign advisers turned out to be as useful to the new government as to him; pushed by the ministers of the new court, he presented his petition on 14 October 1867 offering the government back to the emperor. The immediate occasion came in the first month of the first year of Meiji: the shogunate opened Edo of its own accord, Yoshinobu filed his resignation on the tenth, the court in Kyoto took over Kanto and Hyōgo, and the defeat at Toba and Fushimi made it a settled fact that the shogunate could no longer resist, so that the war had no way of stopping.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果，首先是把日本的舊藩體制連根拔起。幕府的覆亡讓廢藩置縣得以在官軍的軍事統一下推行：一八六九年起各藩陸續廢藩置縣，一八七一年七月地方行政重整完成，二百餘藩的領地、俸祿與軍隊一次過收歸中央；士族賴以維生的舊年收入在秩祿處分中被折價變成一次性公債，接著一八七六年的廢刀令與警察制度，連武裝的權利本身也一併剝去，舊藩主的家臣集團自此在十年間由社會的中樞變成城市的無業人口。其次是軍制的重寫：戊辰戰爭是日本第一次以雷管步槍與西式野戰炮進行的全國性戰爭，槍械的射程、藥莢的定裝與炮兵的分列，讓以密集隊形與白刃戰為基礎的舊式戰法在戰場上直接失效；官軍在兵庫操練場練出的新式步兵、官修的兵學譯書與小石川工場的仿製槍械，構成日後日本陸軍的裝備底子，一八八〇年的三八大式步槍正是這條線的產物。幕府聘用的法國顧問韋爾尼所建的橫濱造船所與關門砲台，則是日本近代造船與海防的起點。第三是對外關係與北方：佛幕砲擊事件讓新政府在外交上付出代價，也促使其在一八七三年以修好條規的形式重訂與各國的關係；蝦夷共和國崩潰後，一八六九年廢北海道與箱館府、一八六九年設開拓使，北方由戰場轉為移民與開發的前線，箱館的殘留勢力直到一八六九年一月的箱館灣海戰才告清除。第四是記憶與隊伍：戊辰戰爭的舊藩兵在明治政府的裁汰與西南戰爭之後被解散，新軍以農村民兵為主，戊辰世代的老兵成為各鎮台的第一批幹部；對後人而言，戊辰戰爭是日本近代軍隊與近代國家的共同起點，而卡面上那件一八四〇年的法國雷管步槍，正是這個起點上最實在的一件器材。
impactEn: The consequences of the war begin with the fact that it uprooted the old system of domains. With the shogunate gone, the abolition of the domains and the creation of prefectures could be carried out under the unity of the government army: from 1869 the domains were abolished one after another, the local administration was reorganised in July 1871, and the territories, stipends and armies of more than two hundred domains passed in a single stroke to the centre. The old income on which the warrior class lived was turned by the commutation of stipends into a one-off bond, and then the abolition of the carrying of swords in 1876 and the police system stripped the right to bear arms itself away, so that within ten years the retainers of the former lords went from the pivot of society to the unemployed of the towns. The second consequence was the rewriting of the military system. The Boshin War was the first nationwide war fought in Japan with percussion muskets and Western field guns; the reach of the rifle, the fixed cartridge and the deployment of artillery made the old style of warfare, based on dense formations and bayonet work, fail outright on the field. The new infantry drilled on the training ground at Hyōgo, the translations of military manuals produced under official auspices, and the copied muskets of the Koishikawa arsenal together formed the equipment basis of the future Japanese army, and the Type 38 rifle of 1880 grew out of that line. The Yokosuka shipyard and the Shimonoseki batteries built for the shogunate by the French adviser Verny were the beginning of modern Japanese shipbuilding and coastal defence. Third came foreign relations and the north. The French-shogunate incident of 1868 made the new government pay a diplomatic price and pushed it to renegotiate its relations with the powers through the treaty of 1873; after the collapse of the Republic of Ezo, Hokkaidō and the Hakodate office were reorganised in 1869 and the Development Commission opened that year, and the north turned from a battlefield into a frontier of migration and settlement, the last Ezo force at Hakodate not being dispersed until the battle of Hakodate Bay in January 1869. Fourth, memory and manpower: the old domain troops were disbanded after the government's reductions and the war in the south-west, the new army was recruited from peasant militia, and the veterans of 1868 became the first officers of the regional commands. For later generations the Boshin War is the common starting point of the modern Japanese army and the modern Japanese state, and the French percussion rifle of 1840 on this card is one of the most concrete objects on that starting line.
result: 結果是幕府體制在六個月內從關西到北海道逐一崩解。元年正月三日江戶城開城，慶喜退守大坂；一月二十七日鳥羽伏見之戰，幕府在官軍兩翼的同時攻擊下損失慘重；五月九日大坂城陷落，慶喜北走，五列車把幕府的殘兵與火炮沿東海道推到敦賀、金澤，而仙台、米澤兩藩於五月相繼倒戈，東北同盟只剩會津一藩硬撐，於六月在奧羽與越中接連失守。北方方面，官軍以先鋒隊在渡島半島登陸，六月第二次總攻擊奪下定頭山，蝦夷共和國於六月二十七日投降，榊莫齊被解送江戶。戰爭的勝負並非由任何一場會戰決定，而是由炮兵、藥莢與彈藥存量決定：官軍在每一處戰場都保有數量可觀的西式野戰炮與定裝藥莢，幕府則在北撤途中丟掉了大部分火炮，最後以步兵與浪人的白刃衝鋒去對抗有槍陣與砲陣的官軍，因此越往北走越難支撐。戰後的結局是一個新國家：新政府接管了關東、關西與北方，元年七月江戶改稱東京，箱館與松前的殘局在翌年被清除，殘存的西南問題在數年後爆發為一八七七年的西南戰爭。戊辰戰爭因此成為日本由幕藩體制走向中央集權國家的分水嶺，而最後一場戰鬥的落幕地，不在關西，而在北海道海峽。
resultEn: The result was that the shogunate system came apart piece by piece within six months, from Kansai to Hokkaidō. On 3 January of the first year of Meiji Edo castle was opened and Yoshinobu fell back on Osaka; on 27 January, at Toba and Fushimi, the shogunate was mauled by a simultaneous attack on both wings; on 9 May Osaka castle fell, Yoshinobu went north, and the five trains carried the shogunate's remnants and guns up the Tōkaidō to Tsuruga and Kanazawa, while Sendai and Yonezawa turned their coats in May, leaving Aizu alone in the Tōhoku alliance and losing Dewa and Echizen in June. In the north the government landed the vanguard on the Oshima peninsula, took the heights of Teitoyama in the second general assault of June, and on 27 June the Republic of Ezo surrendered, Enomoto Takeaki being sent to Edo. The issue of the war was settled by no single engagement, but by artillery, cartridges and the amount of ammunition in the magazine: the government held a substantial number of Western field guns and fixed cartridges at every battlefield, while the shogunate lost most of its artillery on the retreat and finally charged with bayonets, infantry and masterless swordsmen against government troops who had both a line of muskets and a line of guns, which is why the further north it went the harder it was to hold. What stood at the end of the war was a new state: the new government held Kanto, Kansai and the north, Edo was renamed Tokyo in the seventh month of the first year of Meiji, the remnant business at Hakodate and Matsumae was cleared up the following year, and the unresolved question in the south-west broke out as the war of 1877. The Boshin War thus marks the divide between the shogunate-and-domain order and a centralised Japanese state, and the last fighting of the war ended not in Kansai but in the straits of Hokkaidō.
